bull.t: Strong recurring revenue and ARR growth
bull.b: Subscription-based revenue provides recurring demand, while 25% ARR and revenue growth indicates continued customer adoption. This combination supports durable expansion as customers add users, workloads, security modules and Zero Trust capabilities.

bull.t: Broad platform adoption and product expansion
bull.b: Adoption across users, applications, workloads and branches strengthens Zscaler’s platform position and increases cross-sell potential. Broader deployments can deepen customer integration, improve retention and support larger contract values over time.

bull.t: High-margin model with strong cash generation
bull.b: High gross margins and substantial operating cash flow demonstrate attractive software economics and internal funding capacity. Strong free cash flow can support product investment, infrastructure expansion and acquisitions without relying heavily on external capital.

bear.b: Despite improving margins, persistent GAAP losses and modest EBITDA conversion show that the company has not yet demonstrated durable accounting profitability. This may constrain flexibility if growth investments remain elevated or operating leverage develops slowly.

bear.t: Organic growth is expected to decelerate
bear.b: A shift from roughly mid-20% growth toward mid-teens growth would reduce the pace of recurring revenue expansion. Slower organic new-business contribution could also make future growth more dependent on cross-selling, execution and acquisitions.

bear.t: Higher infrastructure spending will pressure cash conversion
bear.b: Higher data-center and branch equipment costs increase the capital intensity of the cloud platform and reduce near-term free cash flow margins. If supply constraints and AI-related component inflation persist, operating leverage and cash conversion may take longer to improve.
